stem: A 10-year-old boy at sexual maturity rating 5 with hyperpigmentation, short stature and a height age below chronological age most likely has
options: Precocious puberty from congenital adrenal hyperplasia, with premature epiphyseal fusion
explanation: Excess adrenal androgen accelerates maturation, so the child is tall as a child but short as an adult. Hyperpigmentation reflects high ACTH. Bone age exceeds chronological age — the opposite of growth hormone deficiency.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (10-year-old, SMR-5, hyperpigmentation, short stature)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: The commonest inherited bleeding disorder is
explanation: It is autosomal, affects both sexes and causes mucocutaneous bleeding with a prolonged bleeding time and often a mildly raised aPTT. Haemophilia A is the commonest **severe** inherited disorder but is less prevalent overall.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (most common inherited bleeding disorder — von Willebrand disease)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Parvovirus B19 in children can cause all of the following EXCEPT
options: Transient aplastic crisis in sickle cell disease
explanation: The virus infects erythroid progenitors, so it causes **production failure**, not haemolysis. In a child with an already shortened red cell lifespan, a brief arrest of production precipitates an aplastic crisis.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (parvovirus causes pure red cell aplasia, hydrops fetalis, transient aplastic crisis)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A child with anaemia, myocarditis, high-output cardiac failure and ascites most likely has infection with
explanation: Severe anaemia drives the high-output failure, and the virus can also cause a direct myocarditis. Erythema infectiosum with a slapped-cheek rash is the common benign presentation in the immunocompetent child.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (anaemia, myocarditis, high output heart failure, ascites — parvovirus B19)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: An 11-month-old boy has recurrent bloody stools, atopic dermatitis and petechiae with small platelets. The gene to screen is
explanation: Wiskott–Aldrich syndrome is the X-linked triad of eczema, thrombocytopenia with characteristically **small** platelets, and immunodeficiency. *BTK* causes X-linked agammaglobulinaemia and *CYBB* chronic granulomatous disease.
exam: 2021 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (recurrent bloody stools, atopic dermatitis, petechiae — screen for WASP gene, 2X)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A child complains of back pain and sweating partway through a blood transfusion. The first action is
options: Slow the transfusion and give an antihistamine
explanation: Back pain, fever and haemoglobinuria suggest an acute haemolytic reaction from ABO incompatibility. The line is kept for saline, the unit and patient identity rechecked, and the bag returned to the blood bank.
exam: 2014 AIIMS (back pain and sweating during blood transfusion — stop the transfusion)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Children with **germline** retinoblastoma are at increased risk of
explanation: The *RB1* tumour suppressor is lost in every cell, so a second malignancy — classically osteosarcoma, and raised further by radiotherapy — follows in survivors. Germline disease is bilateral or multifocal and presents earlier.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (children with germline retinoblastoma can develop osteosarcoma)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Cerebellar haemangioblastoma with renal cell carcinoma indicates
explanation: Autosomal dominant loss of the *VHL* tumour suppressor on chromosome 3p. Retinal and CNS haemangioblastomas, clear cell renal carcinoma, phaeochromocytoma and pancreatic cysts make up the syndrome.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (cerebellar haemangioblastoma with RCC — von Hippel Lindau syndrome)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Ganciclovir resistance in cytomegalovirus arises from mutations in
options: *UL97* kinase and the viral DNA polymerase
explanation: Ganciclovir needs phosphorylation by the viral *UL97* kinase, so loss of that function confers resistance; polymerase mutations give higher-grade resistance. Foscarnet and cidofovir do not require this activation.
exam: 2015 AIIMS (ganciclovir resistance in CMV due to mutation in UL97 gene and DNA polymerase), 2020 INI-CET (commonest cause of infection post solid organ transplantation — CMV, 2X)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A 6-month-old has coryza for 2 days then wheeze, tachypnoea and hyperinflation. The treatment is
options: Supportive care with oxygen and feeding support
explanation: Acute bronchiolitis, usually respiratory syncytial virus, does not respond to bronchodilators, steroids or antibiotics. Minimal handling, oxygen for saturations below about 90% and nasogastric or intravenous fluids are what help.
exam: 2014 AIIMS (palivizumab for RSV), 2021 INI-CET (acute asthma management in children)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Neonatal hypoglycaemia is conventionally treated when the blood glucose falls below
options: 45 mg/dL, with intravenous dextrose if symptomatic or below 25 mg/dL
explanation: Preterm, growth-restricted, macrosomic and infant-of-diabetic-mother babies are screened routinely. A 2 mL/kg bolus of 10% dextrose is followed by an infusion; glucose above 10 to 12 mg/kg/min suggests hyperinsulinism.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (complications in infant of diabetic mother — hypocalcaemia), 2018 AIIMS (investigations in baby of diabetic mother)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A preterm baby on feeds develops abdominal distension, bloody stools and pneumatosis intestinalis on radiography. The diagnosis and management are
options: Necrotising enterocolitis; stop feeds, nasogastric decompression, antibiotics and surgery for perforation
Volvulus; immediate laparotomy in all cases
explanation: Prematurity is the dominant risk factor. Portal venous gas and pneumoperitoneum are ominous, and breast milk with careful feed advancement is protective. Bell staging guides management.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (congenital diaphragmatic hernia), 2023 INI-CET (neonatal sepsis — *Streptococcus agalactiae*)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Screening for retinopathy of prematurity should begin
options: At 4 weeks of age or 31 weeks corrected gestational age, whichever is later
Only if the baby received oxygen
explanation: Babies below 34 weeks or 2,000 g are screened. Uncontrolled oxygen is the key modifiable risk, and treatment is laser photocoagulation or intravitreal anti-VEGF for threshold disease.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (lanugo and prematurity), 2024 INI-CET (iNO and neonatal oxygen therapy)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Kangaroo mother care requires
options: Continuous skin-to-skin contact with exclusive breastfeeding in a stable low-birth-weight baby
Separation from the mother for monitoring
explanation: It reduces mortality, hypothermia, infection and length of stay, and improves breastfeeding and weight gain. It is one of the highest-yield low-cost interventions in newborn care.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (ideal delivery room temperature), 2021 INI-CET (signs of good attachment to breast, 4X)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Apnoea of prematurity is treated with
options: Caffeine citrate, with CPAP for recurrent episodes
explanation: Caffeine has a wider therapeutic window than theophylline and also reduces bronchopulmonary dysplasia and cerebral palsy. Apnoea beginning after the first day of life must prompt a search for sepsis, hypoglycaemia or haemorrhage.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (INSURE in RDS), 2023 INI-CET (free flow oxygen delivery in neonates)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Exchange transfusion in neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia is indicated by
options: A bilirubin above the exchange threshold for gestation and age, or any sign of acute bilirubin encephalopathy
A bilirubin above 15 mg/dL in all babies
Failure of phototherapy after 24 hours in all cases
explanation: Lethargy, poor feeding, hypertonia with retrocollis and a high-pitched cry are the warning signs. Kernicterus causes choreoathetoid cerebral palsy, sensorineural deafness and upgaze palsy.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (4-day-old with bilirubin 18 — phototherapy, 2X), 2017 AIIMS (jaundice on first day of life)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: The commonest organism in **late-onset** neonatal sepsis in a hospital setting is
explanation: Late-onset sepsis after 72 hours is usually nosocomial and line-related, whereas early-onset sepsis reflects maternal flora — group B *Streptococcus*, *Escherichia coli* and *Listeria*. Hand hygiene is the main preventive measure.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (*Streptococcus agalactiae* causes neonatal sepsis), 2021 INI-CET (order of neonatal mortality — prematurity, sepsis, asphyxia)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia is defined as
options: A need for supplemental oxygen at 36 weeks corrected gestational age in a preterm infant
Respiratory distress in the first 6 hours of life
explanation: Volutrauma, oxygen toxicity and inflammation cause it, so gentle ventilation, early CPAP and caffeine reduce it. Vitamin A and, in selected babies, low-dose dexamethasone are used.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (INSURE technique in RDS), 2019 NEET-PG (type 2 alveolar cells in RDS)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Under India's Universal Immunisation Programme, measles–rubella vaccine is given at
options: 9 to 12 months, with a second dose at 16 to 24 months
explanation: BCG, zero-dose OPV and hepatitis B are given at birth; pentavalent with OPV and rotavirus at 6, 10 and 14 weeks; IPV at 6 and 14 weeks. National schedules change by government order, so verify against the current one.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (baby vaccinated at birth and 14 weeks — MR and vitamin A at 9 months), 2023 INI-CET (vaccines for an unimmunised 18-month-old, 3X)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: BCG vaccine is given
options: Intradermally over the left upper arm, and protects mainly against disseminated tuberculosis and tuberculous meningitis
Subcutaneously over the thigh, protecting against pulmonary tuberculosis
Intramuscularly, protecting against all forms of tuberculosis
explanation: Protection against adult pulmonary tuberculosis is poor, which is the point the past papers test. A papule appearing at 2 to 3 weeks and scarring by 6 to 12 weeks is the expected response.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (BCG provides effective protection for disseminated TB, not pulmonary TB)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Vitamin A prophylaxis in India is given as
options: 100,000 IU at 9 months, then 200,000 IU six-monthly up to 5 years
explanation: Vitamin A reduces measles mortality and prevents xerophthalmia, with Bitot spots and night blindness as early signs. Programme doses change by government order.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (MR and oral vitamin A at 9 completed months), 2015 AIIMS (milk deficient in vitamin D)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Iron deficiency anaemia in a child is treated with elemental iron at
options: 3 to 6 mg/kg/day, continued for 2 to 3 months after the haemoglobin normalises
Intravenous iron as first line in all children
explanation: Continuation replenishes stores. A reticulocyte rise within a week confirms response, and failure to respond suggests poor adherence, continuing loss, malabsorption or a wrong diagnosis such as thalassaemia trait.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (most common inherited bleeding disorder), 2015 AIIMS (undernutrition definitions)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A 9-month-old has pallor, hepatosplenomegaly, a haemoglobin of 5 g/dL with a low MCV and raised HbF on electrophoresis. The diagnosis is
explanation: Presentation after 6 months coincides with the switch from fetal to adult haemoglobin. Regular transfusion with iron chelation is standard; untreated children develop the chipmunk facies of extramedullary haematopoiesis.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (inherited bleeding disorder), 2024 INI-CET (parvovirus and aplastic crisis)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A well child develops petechiae and bruising 2 weeks after a viral illness, with a platelet count of 15,000/µL and an otherwise normal blood film. The management is
options: Observation, with IVIG or steroids only for significant bleeding
explanation: Childhood immune thrombocytopenia usually remits spontaneously, so treatment is driven by bleeding rather than by the count. Platelet transfusion is reserved for life-threatening haemorrhage because transfused platelets are destroyed rapidly.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (Wiskott–Aldrich with petechiae, 2X), 2014 AIIMS (transfusion reaction)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: The commonest malignancy of childhood is
explanation: It accounts for about a quarter of childhood cancer, peaking at 2 to 5 years with pallor, fever, bruising, bone pain and organomegaly. Brain tumours are the commonest **solid** tumours. Cure rates now exceed 85%.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (germline retinoblastoma and osteosarcoma), 2018 AIIMS (Wilms tumour features)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome in a child is defined by
options: Remission within 4 weeks of daily prednisolone at 2 mg/kg/day
explanation: Frequent relapses mean two or more in 6 months; steroid dependence means relapse on tapering. Failure to remit by 4 to 6 weeks defines resistance and is an indication for biopsy and genetic testing.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (vaccination in steroid resistant nephrotic syndrome, 2X), 2015 AIIMS (minimal change disease)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: After a first febrile urinary tract infection in an infant, the imaging usually recommended first is
options: Ultrasound of the kidneys, ureters and bladder
explanation: A micturating cystourethrogram is reserved for abnormal ultrasound, atypical or recurrent infection, and is the test that grades vesicoureteric reflux. DMSA scanning detects cortical scarring and is done after the acute episode.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (true about UTI in children, 2X), 2022 INI-CET (posterior urethral valves)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Delayed puberty is defined as absence of breast development by
options: 13 years in girls, and absence of testicular enlargement by 14 years in boys
11 years in girls and 12 years in boys
16 years in girls and 17 years in boys
explanation: Precocious puberty is onset before 8 years in girls and 9 years in boys. Constitutional delay with a positive family history and a delayed bone age is the commonest benign cause.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (SMR-5 with short stature), 2014 AIIMS (DOC for precocious puberty — GnRH analogues)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: In a short child, a bone age **less** than chronological age with a normal growth velocity suggests
options: Constitutional delay or an endocrine cause, rather than a skeletal dysplasia
explanation: Bone age is **normal** in familial short stature and **delayed** in constitutional delay, hypothyroidism and growth hormone deficiency — the single most useful discriminator in the short-stature workup.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (short stature with US/LS ratio 0.8), 2020 INI-CET (height age and chronological age)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A toddler cries, holds his breath, becomes cyanosed and briefly loses consciousness after a minor injury, recovering fully within a minute. The diagnosis is
explanation: A clear provoking event with crying before the event and rapid full recovery distinguishes it from seizure. Iron deficiency is associated and worth correcting; parents need reassurance that spells are benign and self-limiting.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (simple febrile seizure criteria), 2021 INI-CET (juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, 2X)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: In a child with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis, a Mantoux test is considered positive at an induration of
options: 10 mm or more at 48 to 72 hours
5 mm or more in all children
15 mm or more in all children
explanation: A 5 mm threshold applies in immunosuppression and HIV. The test indicates **infection**, not disease, and is unreliable in severe malnutrition, measles and miliary tuberculosis, where it may be falsely negative.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (CSF findings in tubercular meningitis), 2016 AIIMS (BCG and disseminated TB)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Developmental dysplasia of the hip is screened for in a newborn by
options: The Ortolani and Barlow manoeuvres, with ultrasound if abnormal or risk factors are present
Plain radiography at birth in all babies
explanation: Barlow dislocates a dislocatable hip and Ortolani relocates a dislocated one. Breech presentation, female sex, oligohydramnios and a family history are the risk factors; radiography is unhelpful before the femoral head ossifies.
exam: 2015 AIIMS (prune belly and oligohydramnios-related deformity), 2024 INI-CET (developmental assessment)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: The first permanent teeth to erupt, at about 6 years, are the
explanation: Primary dentition begins with the lower central incisors at about 6 months and completes with 20 teeth by about 2.5 years. Delayed eruption suggests hypothyroidism, rickets or Down syndrome.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (anterior fontanelle closure), 2023 INI-CET (head circumference growth)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Systemic-onset juvenile idiopathic arthritis is characterised by
options: Quotidian fever with an evanescent salmon-pink rash, hepatosplenomegaly and serositis
Symmetrical small joint arthritis with rheumatoid factor
explanation: Macrophage activation syndrome is its feared complication, marked by a **falling** ESR with a very high ferritin. Option D describes rheumatic fever, the main differential.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (molecular mimicry in rheumatic fever), 2023 INI-CET (IgA vasculitis management)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: In acute rheumatic carditis with heart failure, the treatment is
options: Penicillin to eradicate the organism, with anti-inflammatory therapy and heart failure management
explanation: Corticosteroids are generally preferred to aspirin when carditis causes failure. Eradication does not alter the current attack but prevents reinfection, which is why secondary prophylaxis follows immediately.
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (benzathine penicillin prophylaxis duration), 2023 INI-CET (Nadas criteria, 2X)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Severe falciparum malaria in a child is treated with
options: Intravenous artesunate, followed by a full oral artemisinin-based combination course
explanation: Artesunate reduced mortality against quinine in the AQUAMAT trial in African children. Hypoglycaemia, severe anaemia and convulsions are commoner in children than in adults with severe malaria.
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (pertussis treatment), 2024 INI-CET (tubercular meningitis)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: In dengue in a child, the phase of greatest danger is
options: The critical phase around the time of defervescence, when plasma leakage occurs
explanation: A rising haematocrit with a falling platelet count and narrowing pulse pressure signals leakage. Careful crystalloid titration is the treatment; fluid overload during the recovery phase is the common iatrogenic harm.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (rotavirus and dehydration assessment), 2014 AIIMS (paediatric shock — 20 mL/kg normal saline)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A child has honey-coloured crusted lesions around the mouth with no systemic upset. The diagnosis and treatment are
options: Impetigo; topical mupirocin, with oral antibiotics if extensive
explanation: *Staphylococcus aureus* and group A *Streptococcus* are responsible. It is highly contagious, so the child stays off school until crusts dry. Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis can follow streptococcal impetigo.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (identify the condition — intertrigo), 2021 INI-CET (post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Nutritional rickets is treated with
options: Vitamin D with adequate calcium, followed by a maintenance dose
Active vitamin D (calcitriol) in all cases
explanation: Calcium must accompany vitamin D or hungry-bone hypocalcaemia can follow. Calcitriol is reserved for renal failure and vitamin D-dependent rickets, where 1-alpha-hydroxylation is the defective step.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (nutritional rickets biochemistry), 2021 NEET-PG (hypophosphataemic rickets)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Autism spectrum disorder in a toddler is suggested by
options: Failure to point to show interest, absent joint attention and no response to name by 12 to 18 months
explanation: Loss of previously acquired language or social skills at any age is a red flag demanding immediate referral. Hearing assessment is part of every evaluation of social and language delay.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (9-month-old developmental assessment), 2022 INI-CET (spoon feeding delay at 3 years, 2X)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: The commonest cause of neonatal mortality in India, in descending order, is
options: Prematurity and low birth weight, then sepsis, then birth asphyxia, then congenital anomaly
Congenital anomaly, then sepsis, then prematurity
Birth asphyxia, then prematurity, then sepsis
explanation: Neonatal deaths make up about two-thirds of infant mortality, and most occur in the first week. This ordering drives the design of newborn care programmes.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (arrange in decreasing order of mortality in neonates)

subject: Pediatrics
stem: The most reliable sign that a baby is receiving enough breast milk is
options: Adequate weight gain with at least six wet nappies a day
The baby sleeping through the night
The mother's perception of breast fullness
Feeding fewer than six times a day
explanation: Output and weight are objective; maternal perception of supply is not. A weight loss of more than 7 to 10% of birth weight, or failure to regain birth weight by 2 weeks, needs feeding assessment.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (signs of good attachment to breast, 4X), 2019 NEET-PG (best sign of adequate growth)
